jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking a research scientist who combines deep chemistry knowledge with machine learning expertise to join the team. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be a computational chemist who knows reactions, synthesis, and medicinal chemistry in depth and has hands-on experience training and evaluating machine learning models. Above all, you'll build the reinforcement learning environments, datasets, and evaluations that teach Claude chemistry. Working alongside our bench chemists and AI researchers, you'll turn real chemistry problems and experimental data into training tasks and measure whether the models get better at them.

This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* Design and build reinforcement learning environments for chemistry end to end, including task design, data curation, automated grading, and checks against shortcuts and data leakage
* Design and source new experimental datasets, environments, and evaluations with our bench chemists, and external research and academic partners
* Develop evaluations that measure model performance on real chemistry tasks, such as reaction outcome prediction, synthesis planning, structure elucidation, and compound design, and feed results back to research teams
* Run and analyze training experiments with AI research teams, diagnose where models fail at chemistry, and prioritize what to build next
* Ensure datasets and environments are high quality and well documented, including sources, train and test splits, and failure modes
* Communicate findings clearly to chemistry, AI research, and life sciences audiences

**Minimum qualifications**
--------------------------

* PhD in chemistry, computational chemistry, or a related field
* Deep knowledge of organic and medicinal chemistry, including reactions, synthesis, and SAR, with experimental data as your ground truth
* Strong Python skills and solid machine learning fundamentals, with hands-on experience training and evaluating models
* Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills

**Preferred qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience with reinforcement learning, large language models, or building evaluations and benchmarks
* Track record of supporting drug discovery programs alongside medicinal and synthetic chemists
* Experience curating chemistry datasets from the literature, patents, or lab notebooks, including reaction, ADMET, and spectroscopic data
* Cheminformatics and molecular modeling skills, for example RDKit, docking, free energy calculations, or quantum chemistry
* Hands-on synthetic or medicinal chemistry experience at the bench

Data Science - San Francisco

**About the Team**

We work across product, growth, and monetization to help people get more value from OpenAI’s products. We identify opportunities for machine learning, build and test early solutions, and partner with engineering and product to bring successful approaches into production.

**About the Role**

We’re looking for a data scientist who can enter an unfamiliar product area, find a useful ML application, and turn it into a working product intervention. You will own the work from problem definition and data preparation through modeling, experimentation, and launch evaluation.

Projects will include personalization, next-best-action recommendations, lifecycle management, promotion targeting, and models of retention and customer lifetime value. You will help identify opportunities, build proofs of concept, evaluate, and iterate.

**In this role, you will:**

* Identify opportunities with product and business partners, and prioritize work by user value, feasibility, and expected impact.
* Build datasets, features, reproducible training workflows, and models. You’ll use a combination of tools appropriate to the task at hand.
* Translate predictions into product actions. Design experiments and use causal reasoning to establish whether those actions improve user and business outcomes.
* Partner with engineers on integration, serving or batch scoring, monitoring, and rollout. Stay involved through launch and iteration.
* Explain results and limitations clearly, document decisions, and build reusable methods that other teams can adopt.

**You might thrive in this role if you:**

* Have built and evaluated applied ML systems that influenced a product or business decision, with clear ownership of the modeling work.
* Write effective Python and SQL and can investigate imperfect data, debug models, and make pragmatic implementation choices.
* Build and schedule production scoring pipelines using dbt, airflow, and flyte.
* Understand supervised learning, evaluation, experimentation, and the difference between predicting an outcome and changing it.
* Can scope ambiguous problems, work across disciplines, and explain technical tradeoffs to colleagues with different backgrounds.
* Are motivated by helping people use AI effectively and by learning unfamiliar product domains.
* Are excited to take on challenging, impactful ML problems across multiple areas.
* Have experience with recommendation systems, personalization, growth, retention, lifetime value, or treatment-effect modeling would be useful. We welcome candidates whose relevant experience comes from other domains.

jobs.description:
**Software Engineer, Infrastructure**
=====================================

**Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) · $185K–$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits**

**About Sodalis**
-----------------

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.  
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.  
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.
* Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.
* Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.
* Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.
* Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.
* You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.
* You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.
* You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.
* You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.
* You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

**How we work**
---------------

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.

Compensation Range: $185K - $215K

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Generative UI, Input Experience
jobs.description:
A generated interface is only as good as the pieces it's made from. Give a model the wrong pieces and it fails, producing something generic or broken. Give it the right ones and it can make something a designer would be proud of.  
  
We're looking for an engineer with a designer's eye to build those pieces: the views, layouts, and APIs that generated interfaces are built from. The goal is to make the right result the easy one to write, for people and models.  
  
**Description**  
  
You'll join a small, newly formed team working closely with Apple's design studio, and you'll own the UI layer that generative interfaces are built on. Your APIs will have two kinds of users: engineers, and the models generating interfaces in real time. Most of the work is finding the right abstraction. Which layout decisions should a view make by itself? Which should be stated as intent? Which should never be exposed at all? An API that answers those questions well lets a model write a few lines and get something that feels native.  
  
The hard cases are the ones designers usually solve by hand: tight space, many sizes, content whose length and shape aren't known until it arrives. You'll build components that handle them without anyone drawing each one.  
  
With designers, you'll prototype quickly until something feels right, then turn it into a principled, well-named API with a small surface. With the generation side, you'll study how models use your APIs and change them until good results are the default. Along the way you'll partner with design, AI, and UI framework teams across Apple.  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**  
  
Experience designing framework API: naming, progressive disclosure, defaults  
  
Experience building adaptive layouts that stay correct with content that isn't known ahead of time  
  
Deep knowledge of Dynamic Type, accessibility, localization, and right-to-left layout  
  
Experience building or maintaining a design system or component library used across many product teams  
  
Experience designing APIs or schemas that a model generates against  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**  
  
5+ years of software engineering experience  
  
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience  
  
Expert-level SwiftUI, including custom Layout and preferences, with a deep understanding of its layout model  
  
Designed and shipped a reusable view or component API that other engineers adopted  
  
A portfolio, shipped work, or prototypes that show strong visual craft, especially typography and layout  
  
Comfortable working directly with designers, from early ambiguous exploration through to a pixel-exact result

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building robotic systems that combine frontier AI, sophisticated control, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is an opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction.
  
  
We are seeking an Applied Scientist to develop tactile- and force-driven manipulation policies for highly dexterous, multi-fingered robotic hands and grippers. In this role you will research and build policy learning algorithms that enable robotic hands to perform grasping and in-hand manipulation in unstructured, real-world environments, using touch and force feedback as first-class signals rather than afterthoughts. Much of this work is grounded in reinforcement learning.
  
  
To be successful you need to be highly motivated, dive deep, and deliver to the highest standards. You will demonstrate strong working knowledge of modern policy learning methods, with expertise in taking algorithms from simulation onto real hardware. That means being comfortable working against real physical constraints and treating sim-to-real as a core research problem rather than optimizing for benchmark numbers alone. You will work across tactile signal processing, contact-rich manipulation, sim-to-real transfer, and multi-modal sensor fusion to build robust solutions for autonomous grasping, dexterous re-orientation, and fine motor control. You will bring the desire to learn from new challenges, and the problem-solving and communication skills to work within a highly interactive and experienced team.
  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Design and train manipulation policies that leverage tactile and force feedback for dexterous grasping, in-hand manipulation, and contact-rich tasks, using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or hybrid approaches.
* Drive sim-to-real transfer, closing the gap between simulated and physical performance on real robotic hands.
* Shape objectives and control strategies with the hardware in mind, accounting for how motors and actuators actually behave: transmission ratios, torque versus power, backdrivability, and thermal limits.
* Build simulation-based and on-robot evaluation frameworks, with benchmarks and metrics that make tactile perception and policy performance systematically comparable across iterations.
* Own scientific and technical projects within the tactile sensing and manipulation workstreams, driving from research concept through deployment on physical robotic systems — and, at the senior level, set direction across a workstream.
* Collaborate with hardware, mechanical design, firmware, and controls teams — and with partner applied science organizations — to translate research advances into deployable robotic capabilities, and to inform sensor and actuator design decisions with policy-level requirements.
* Publish at top-tier venues and build collaborations with the external research community.
* Contribute to a strong scientific bar on the team through code and design review, and mentor engineers and interns working on real-world manipulation and sensing problems.

  
A day in the life  
Your morning might start with a standup alongside hardware and controls engineers reviewing overnight sim-to-real training runs on a multi-finger gripper, debugging why a grasp policy that worked in simulation is slipping on a real sensor array. Mid-morning you join the weekly tactile sensing workstream to align on sensor integration milestones and share early results from a contact-state estimator you have been prototyping.
